vedic_reference.note: Vedas are the ancient Hindu scriptures, while आनन्द (anand) means 'bliss' or 'joy'.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vedanand holds deep roots in Hindu culture and is associated with ancient knowledge and wisdom passed down through generations. Scholars and spiritual teachers bearing this name have significantly contributed to preserving and disseminating the Vedas, the sacred Hindu texts. Vedanand possesses a profound reverence for learning and the wisdom that comes with it.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Vedanand signifies the ultimate attainment of spiritual knowledge and the resulting profound joy or bliss, about which Hindu scriptures speak. The union of Veda (knowledge) and Anand (bliss) denotes the understanding that true wisdom and inner peace come from the harmonious blend of the Intellect and the Divine. The bearer of this name is understood to strive for the experiential realization of this invigorating unity in life.

historical_references.reference: Vedanand was a prominent Hindu monk and scholar during the Gupta Empire (circa 4th to 6th century CE). He is known for his extensive knowledge of the Vedas and his contributions to their interpretation and preservation.
historical_references.context: Gupta Empire, Hinduism, Vedas, Monk, Scholar, Interpretation, Preservation

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Vedanand comes from the 13th century Jain text, 'Kalpa Sutra'. In this text, Vedanand is described as a great teacher and a leader of the Jain community. He is also credited with composing several Jain texts, including the 'Tattvartha Sutra'.
historical_references.context: Jainism, Teacher, Leader, Composer, Tattvartha Sutra
